units.title: Successful stopped executions have one output and count

sources.label: Chen–Chewi–Lu–Zhang, stopped routine and actual Picard query centers
sources.scope: Conditional deterministic identity for successful runs only. No existence of a successful run, proximal accuracy, count bound, Gaussian law or main theorem. Reusable interface extracted for the same-witness full-phase consumer; no independent paper-progress credit for extraction.

assumptions: E is a real normed vector space; g:E->E, eta,eps,y and initial state x are arbitrary. Two supplied finite fuels n,m yield successful returned pairs r,s under the same deterministic interpreter. No positivity, contractivity or termination hypothesis.
units.statement: For the deterministic stopped gradient interpreter of Algorithm D.2, any two successful finite-fuel executions from the same y and initial x, using the same g,eta,eps, return exactly the same pair (output point, actual gradient-test count), independently of the sufficient fuels.
units.boundary: Conditional deterministic identity for successful runs only. No existence of a successful run, proximal accuracy, count bound, Gaussian law or main theorem. Reusable interface extracted for the same-witness full-phase consumer; no independent paper-progress credit for extraction.

steps.title: Exclude zero fuel
steps.text: Zero fuel returns none, so a supplied successful run cannot have zero fuel. Induct on the first fuel and eliminate zero fuel for the second.
steps.lean: induction n; cases m; simp [proximalQuery] at hr hs

steps.title: Compare identical stopping branches
steps.text: Both positive-fuel runs evaluate the same gradient at the same current x and the same residual test. If that test succeeds, both return the current x with count one. This counts the final gradient evaluation.

steps.title: Compare identical continuing branches
steps.text: If the common residual test fails, both recurse at the same next point y-eta*g(x). Successful Option.map outputs imply successful recursive returned pairs. The induction hypothesis identifies those pairs; applying the same count increment gives equality of the outer returned pairs. No mathematical contraction or termination claim is needed.

units.lean_statement: Arbitrary real normed E, g, eta, eps, y, x and finite fuels n,m; successful interpreter equations for both returned pairs imply exact equality r=s. No measure or probability law occurs.
units.lean_proof: Induct on the first fuel, eliminate zero successful fuel for either run, then compare the identical residual test. A stopping branch returns the same pair; a continuing branch uses recursive pair equality and the same count increment.
